extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting effective foreshadowing in fiction focused on the two halves: setup (plant) and payoff, plus principles, types, failure modes, and tests to evaluate foreshadowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-Beat Rhythm (Plant → Patience → Payoff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every piece of foreshadowing requires: Plant — early presence (often disguised as ordinary detail); Patience — distance between plant and payoff (often watered with subtle reminders); Payoff — the moment of recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat foreshadowing as a three-part rhythm: plant the seed early, allow time/distance for it to gestate (with occasional subtle reminders), then deliver the payoff so the earlier seed recontextualizes events. Example: The Sixth Sense — scenes where Malcolm seems ignored gain new meaning at the payoff because each scene was meaningful then and payoff-ready.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reverse-Engineering Principle
rubrics_metrics.description: Setup and payoff are written in reverse — the writer comes up with the payoff first, then goes back to find the optimum place to plant the seed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design the twist or outcome first so you can place plants that will both read naturally in their scene and support the future payoff; avoid inventing plants before knowing what they must set up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subtle
rubrics_metrics.description: Subtle — too obvious telegraphs the twist; too hidden feels arbitrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for a level of noticeability where on first read the plant doesn't shout its future role, but on re-read the reader recognizes it. Avoid overt signaling that solves the twist and avoid burying plants so deep they feel contrived at payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional in the moment
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional in the moment — best plants do double duty (have meaning right now AND set up later).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plant details should serve the immediate scene (characterization, plot, mood) so they don't read as inert clues; this both preserves subtlety and justifies the plant's presence before payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Watered along the way
rubrics_metrics.description: "Watered" along the way — subtle reminders keep the seed alive without spotlighting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use gentle callbacks or thematic echoes to keep the plant active across the patience period. These reminders should not draw attention to themselves as clues but should sustain plausibility for the later payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inevitable in retrospect
rubrics_metrics.description: Inevitable in retrospect — readers should think 'Oh, THAT'S what that meant'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strong payoff makes earlier plants feel like they had to be there; the reader should feel the outcome was earned and logically consistent with what came before.

rubrics_metrics.name: Doesn't reduce surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Doesn't reduce surprise — readers know the twist is coming because it's earned, not because they've solved it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreshadowing should heighten eventual surprise by preparing the narrative groundwork without allowing readers to predict the twist prematurely; balance inevitability with moment-of-recognition surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct (heralds)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direct (heralds) — explicit warning (e.g., 'Beware the Ides of March').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use direct foreshadowing when you want a clear forewarning voice or to create dramatic irony; be careful—too explicit can remove suspense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect (hints)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect (hints) — implication via image, dialogue, action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implant subtle clues through sensory details, offhand lines, or small actions that gain meaning later; rely on reader inference rather than outright statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symbolic
rubrics_metrics.description: Symbolic — recurring symbol that prefigures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use motifs or symbols repeated across scenes to build associative meaning that pays off later; ensure the symbol is woven naturally into the narrative so it doesn't feel decorative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atmospheric
rubrics_metrics.description: Atmospheric — mood/weather that signals coming events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create a tone or environmental cue (e.g., storm, oppressive heat) that telegraphs future shifts in plot or emotion; avoid making weather feel like a literal clue if you want to keep subtlety.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chekhov's Gun
rubrics_metrics.description: Chekhov's Gun — object placed early, used later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce objects or details with plausible reasons for their presence, then employ them in the payoff; failure to use such objects is a common broken promise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreshadowing by analogy
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreshadowing by analogy — earlier event mirrors later one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage smaller or analogous incidents earlier to foreshadow a larger later event, creating resonance and thematic echo without explicit signaling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negative foreshadowing
rubrics_metrics.description: Negative foreshadowing — character says 'this will never happen' (then it does).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use denials or confident statements as plants that can be overturned later for irony or thematic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prophecy
rubrics_metrics.description: Prophecy — explicit prediction that comes true (oracular).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prophecies can be literal or subverted; use them to structure expectations or to misdirect—the handling determines whether they feel earned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setup without payoff (broken promise)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failure: Setup without payoff (broken promise / Chekhov's gun unfired).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure every significant plant has a satisfying payoff; leaving plants unredeemed frustrates readers and weakens narrative economy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payoff without setup (deus ex machina)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failure: Payoff without setup (deus ex machina / unearned twist).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid introducing critical elements only at the payoff; a twist must be grounded in earlier material so it doesn't feel arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy-handed setup that telegraphs everything
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failure: Heavy-handed setup that telegraphs everything.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Don't overload scenes with obvious cues that give away the twist; maintain subtlety so readers experience surprise at payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Buried setup that feels random when paid off
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failure: Buried setup that feels random when paid off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plants are too obscure or buried, the payoff will feel unearned; make plants discoverable on re-read without making them obvious on first read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excessive setup ahead of small payoff (front-loaded)
rubrics_metrics.description: Common failure: Excessive setup ahead of small payoff (front-loaded).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Match the scale of setup to the significance of the payoff; avoid spending substantial narrative weight on a minor payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: "Great foreshadowing feels inevitable in hindsight but surprising in the moment."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for the paradoxical balance where the payoff seems both earned and surprising; use plant/patience/watering to achieve this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test — recontextualization after payoff
rubrics_metrics.description: After the payoff, do earlier scenes recontextualize?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A useful diagnostic: if the payoff doesn't change how earlier scenes read, the foreshadowing may be weak or absent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test — plants identifiable on re-read
rubrics_metrics.description: Could the reader, on re-read, identify the plants?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If plants are not discoverable on a careful re-read, the payoff may feel unearned; conversely, if they are too obvious on first read, they may spoil the surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test — sufficient patience period
rubrics_metrics.description: Was the patience period long enough to forget the seed?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow enough distance between plant and payoff that readers don't keep the detail active in mind, yet keep it reachable via subtle watering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Test — watering without obviousness
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the watering keep the seed alive without making it obvious?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that reminders sustain plausibility and memory of the plant without functioning as blatant hints; good watering preserves subtlety while preventing forgetfulness.
